concept.name: Document Database Modeling

relationships.description: Connects Document Database Modeling to database indexing in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Modeling around top access patterns in MongoDB/DynamoDB—embedding bounded 1-to-few subdocs, referencing unbounded children, and indexing with ESR.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of document modeling—from Embedding vs Referencing and the Bucket/Subset patterns to ESR compound indexes and avoiding 16 MiB BSON overflows.

spark.summary: Document database modeling optimizes for read-path locality by co-locating data that is queried together inside self-contained JSON/BSON documents, trading normalized storage for single-round-trip reads.
spark.keyTakeaway: Model documents around application access patterns rather than abstract entity-relationship tables: embed bounded 1-to-few subdocuments, reference unbounded 1-to-many arrays, and respect document size limits (e.g., MongoDB's 16 MiB BSON cap).
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Relational modeling normalizes data assuming joins are cheap. **Document modeling** (MongoDB WiredTiger, AWS DynamoDB) flips that assumption: data **read together should be stored together** in a self-contained JSON/BSON document.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Subset & Extended Reference Patterns Keeping Hot Docs in WiredTiger RAM (GET /orders/:id -> WiredTiger RAM -> order_events Coll -> ESR Compound Index); Compound B-Tree Index Following Equality -> Sort -> Range (E: status = 'PAID' -> S: createdAt DESC -> R: totalCents >= 50 -> IXSCAN 1:1 Ratio).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Select the document pattern matching relationship cardinality. Never shard a document collection on monotonic `createdAt` or `ObjectId` (routes 100% of writes to one shard); use a high-cardinality compound shard key `{ tenantId: 1, entityId.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore DynamoDB hot-partition sharding, monotonic key hotspots, B-Tree vs LSM indexing, and database sharding.

learningJourney.title: What is Document Database Modeling
learningJourney.explanation:
Relational modeling normalizes data assuming joins are cheap. **Document modeling** (MongoDB WiredTiger, AWS DynamoDB) flips that assumption: data **read together should be stored together** in a self-contained JSON/BSON document.

Schema design starts from your **top 5–10 read/write queries**: embed **1-to-1** and **bounded 1-to-few** (`<100` items) subdocuments for single-round-trip reads and single-doc atomicity, and reference **unbounded 1-to-many / 1-to-millions** children in separate collections.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Document Database Modeling works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Unbounded Arrays & `$lookup` Storms Destroy p99 Latency
learningJourney.explanation: Treating MongoDB like a relational DB with `$lookup` everywhere triggers scatter-gather shard joins; conversely, pushing unbounded comments/reviews into an embedded array overflows WiredTiger pages, forces full-doc rewrites, and hits the **16 MiB BSON ceiling**.

sectionDiagram.title: Subset & Extended Reference Patterns Keeping Hot Docs in WiredTiger RAM
sectionDiagram.summary: Keeping hot summary fields + bounded items (~2 KB) in WiredTiger RAM prevents 2 MB blobs from evicting active working sets.

ideas.title: Product Reviews: Fixing 16 MiB BSON Overflow
ideas.description: Popular products hit 15,000 embedded reviews, breaching 16 MiB and spiking writes to 140 ms. Moving reviews to a `reviews` collection while embedding `reviewSummary` + top 3 pinned reviews cut write latency to 4 ms.

ideas.title: IoT Telemetry with the Bucket Pattern
ideas.description: Bucketing 600 readings (10 min) per doc across 10,000 devices cut document count 600x (from 864M/day) and shrank WiredTiger index RAM by 94%.

learningJourney.title: Where Document Modeling Fits (and Where Relational / Graph Wins)
learningJourney.explanation: Choose document stores for hierarchical aggregates and polymorphic catalogs; avoid them for multi-hop graphs or cross-aggregate financial ledgers.

benefits: Orders + line items, product variants without sparse NULLs, single-key JSON reads.
costs: Duplicated Extended Reference fields need Change Stream sync on updates.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Unbounded Append Arrays Inside Parent Docs
benefits: Use the Bucket Pattern or child collection with `{ parentId: 1, ts: -1 }`.
costs: Uncapped `$push` hits 16 MiB BSON limit and fragments storage.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Ad-Hoc Multi-Hop Joins & Multi-Entity Ledgers
benefits: PostgreSQL 3NF or graph engines handle arbitrary joins and multi-row ACID cleanly.
costs: Sharded `$lookup` fans out to all shards.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Apply ESR Indexing, `$jsonSchema` & Schema Versioning
learningJourney.explanation:
1. **ESR Index Rule**: Order compound indexes by **E**quality (`status: 'PAID'`), then **S**ort (`createdAt: -1`), then **R**ange (`amount: {$gte: 50}`). Verify `IXSCAN` and `nReturned / totalDocsExamined >= 0.5` with `.explain('executionStats')`.
2. **Partial & TTL Indexes**: Use `partialFilterExpression` when 95% of docs are archived, shrinking index RAM 20x.
3. **Enforce `$jsonSchema` + `schemaVersion: 2`**: Prevent silent `"42"` vs `42` drift and lazily upgrade `v1` docs in app memory.

costs: Cap via `$jsonSchema` `maxItems` so arrays never grow unbounded.

benefits: Eliminates `$lookup` joins on hot list views.
costs: Requires async Change Stream updates if `customerName` changes.

benefits: Keeps latest 10 items in hot doc; archives 500 historical items in `*_overflow`.
costs: Second query needed only when user clicks 'View full history'.

benefits: Groups 200–600 readings/doc, cutting index RAM by >90%.
costs: Queries slice inside the bucket array in application/aggregation code.

knowledgeCheck.question: You need a MongoDB compound index for `db.orders.find({ tenantId: 't1', amount: { $gte: 100 } }).sort({ createdAt: -1 })`. Which key order follows the ESR rule to avoid an in-memory blocking sort?

options.feedback: Correct: Equality (`tenantId`) narrows the prefix, Sort (`createdAt`) returns results pre-ordered, and Range (`amount`) filters the tail.
Putting a range predicate first forces MongoDB to scan multiple subtrees and perform an in-memory sort.
Without `tenantId` equality first, the index scans across all tenants.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
